subject: Same seed, different compilers, different output

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Same seed, different compilers, different output
parts:
Hi,

I am running the following on two different computers, which have different c++ compilers, and I seem to be getting different results:

fit <- stan(file = aStanModel, data = data, iter = 1000, chains = 1, seed=1)

One computer is a Mac which produces the following under gcc --version:

Configured with: --prefix=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr --with-gxx-include-dir=/usr/include/c++/4.2.1

Apple LLVM version 5.1 (clang-503.0.38) (based on LLVM 3.4svn)

Target: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0

Thread model: posix


The other is a linux machine using:


gcc (GCC) 4.4.7 20120313 (Red Hat 4.4.7-11)


The fit object that is returned in both cases is different - samples, Rhats etc.


Does anyone know what might be causing this difference?


Best,


Ben

parts:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2015 at 11:40 AM, Ben Lambert <ben.c....@googlemail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I am running the following on two different computers, which have different c++ compilers, and I seem to be getting different results:

fit <- stan(file = aStanModel, data = data, iter = 1000, chains = 1, seed=1)

One computer is a Mac which produces the following under gcc --version:

Configured with: --prefix=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr --with-gxx-include-dir=/usr/include/c++/4.2.1

Apple LLVM version 5.1 (clang-503.0.38) (based on LLVM 3.4svn)

Target: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0

Thread model: posix


The other is a linux machine using:


gcc (GCC) 4.4.7 20120313 (Red Hat 4.4.7-11)


The fit object that is returned in both cases is different - samples, Rhats etc.


Does anyone know what might be causing this difference?

Yes. It's the compiler and the architecture.

Stan will reproduce the exact same draws with a fixed seed when the compiled target is the same. This requires:
- same architecture
- same compiler
- same compiler options, especially the optimization level
- same seed

Different compilers might do different things. Even with the "same" compiler (based on version number) across different architectures may produce different results. And we've definitely seen the same compiler, same seed, different optimization levels producing different results.

In your case, there's no reason to believe that you'll reproduce the same thing across different OSs and compilers.


Best,


Ben
